expected_evidence: Geological: independent stratigraphic sampling of the ~12.9 ka Younger Dryas boundary (YDB) layer across multiple North American sites, testing for the claimed impact proxies (nanodiamonds, magnetic/glass spherules, platinum anomaly, elevated iridium, 'black mat' organic layer)

Geological: published re-analyses / blind inter-laboratory comparisons showing failure to reproduce the original proxy concentrations or misidentification of proxies (e.g., framework carbon vs. true nanodiamonds, spherules attributed to non-impact processes)

Material: archaeological correlation data (Clovis-era site abandonment/discontinuity claims) checked against site-by-site chronology to see if the extinction/discontinuity signal is real or coincidental with normal climate-driven change
Astronomical/geophysical: absence of a confirmed impact crater or airburst signature of appropriate age and size in North America despite search efforts

Genetic: megafaunal extinction/population bottleneck timing data used to test (and generally fail to uniquely support) an abrupt catastrophic-impact-driven collapse versus gradual climate-driven decline
Model_prior: theoretical/modeling literature on impact/airburst mechanisms invoked to explain YD cooling, and critiques of the physical plausibility of the proposed mechanism
response.rationale: This hypothesis is a meta-scientific claim: that the proposed cosmic-impact cause of Younger Dryas onset cooling failed independent replication. Unlike most archaeological hypotheses, the relevant 'evidence' here is largely modern scientific literature examining ancient sediment, not fragile perishable artifacts — so its survival depends more on research effort than on taphonomic preservation. The core diagnostic layer (YDB black mat / sediment horizon) is geological and has moderate-to-good preservation potential (younger-dryas geological detectability 0.65), and it has in fact been sampled at dozens of sites by multiple independent teams over the past ~15 years (model-prior: I recall published inter-laboratory studies, e.g. on nanodiamond and spherule proxies, reporting non-reproduction or alternative explanations — this is drawn from training knowledge, not the evidence text provided, so it should be treated as low-tier/unverified until confirmed against primary sources). Material evidence (archaeological site continuity/discontinuity) has lower detectability (0.35) because Paleoindian site records are sparse and dating uncertainties are large, making 'replication failure' harder to demonstrate unambiguously from material remains alone. Genetic evidence bearing on megafaunal extinction timing is only weakly diagnostic for an impact-specific mechanism (genetic 0.3) and mostly supports or refutes indirectly. Astronomical evidence (crater search) has high nominal detectability (0.7) but a lack of a positive crater find is inherently ambiguous — absence of a crater is expected whether or not the impact hypothesis is true, since small/airburst events need not leave a crater, weakening this line's diagnostic power despite good detectability. Overall, because the central evidence type (geological stratigraphy, independently sampled at many sites) is both expected and well within survivable/detectable range, an absence of confirmed independent replication is unlikely to be explained by poor preservation — it is more likely a genuine negative result. I set the composite detectability adjustment at 0.55, reflecting good survivability for the primary geological evidence but discounting for the weaker, more ambiguous secondary lines (material, genetic, astronomical) that would be needed to fully corroborate or refute a replication failure across the whole hypothesis space.
